Purpose and exclusions

Prove the integrated player journey in a real packaged client/server environment, while distinguishing documentation static checks from gameplay verification. Release only the measured, tested scope.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. In Project Settings confirm maps to cook include frontend, the two initial zones and dungeon/test maps only as appropriate to the build. Development-only fixtures and secrets must be excluded from public shipping packages.
  2. Create a release fixture with two accounts, four classes, initial quest chain, merchant, ore/tree sites, fishing pool, craft station and two reciprocal gates.
  3. Use separate client processes/machines and a dedicated process without a local player; multi-PIE is a convenience regression test, not the final remote proof.
  4. Capture server-authoritative coordinates, XP, inventory/currency/quest/profession revisions, ticket epochs and receipt IDs at each route checkpoint.
  5. Force crash before and after transaction commit, destination reservation, ticket redemption and arrival acknowledgment; expected state is in the failure matrix.
  6. Validate controller remapping, readable telegraphs at text scale 150–200%, no color-only rarity meaning, subtitles/visual fishing cues and localized overflow.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in End-to-end testing, packaging and release acceptance. Rule owner: URPGAcceptanceHarness. This asset’s role is Prove the integrated player journey in a real packaged client/server environment, while distinguishing documentation static checks from gameplay verification. Release only the measured, tested scope.

  1. Build development and shipping client/server targets using the installed engine packaging route and actual supported platform toolchain.
  2. Deploy an isolated backend/database and two zone processes from the same release manifest; provision two or more real test accounts.
  3. Execute Slice A, then Slice B, then the online-ready route with party/dungeon/social flows and documented fault injection.
  4. For every economic action, compare UI, authoritative state, database rows and command receipt after retry/disconnect/zone change.
  5. Run navigation/accessibility/localization/layout tests with long text, keyboard-only and controller focus; verify opening menus does not pause the server.
  6. Attach actual observed results, block release on invariant or security failures, and report the largest tested population rather than a theoretical MMO capacity.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / L_Thornweald / L_SluiceVault / separate packaged clients. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Any duplicate grant or dual active session -> ReleaseBlocked, regardless of visual polish.
Client packages but dedicated server fails -> not a multiplayer build pass.
Static docs validator passes -> does not mark Unreal/runtime test Passed.
Two-zone route sends both players away -> fail: individual ClientTravel contract violated.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
